params.question: Why is growth faltering considered one of the earliest warning signs available to paediatricians?

answers.text: It causes visible wasting and oedema within days of onset

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Visible wasting and oedema are late signs of malnutrition. Growth faltering, detected by serial weight plotting, appears well before these become clinically evident.

answers.text: It can be detected by serial weight measurements weeks to months before clinical signs of illness appear

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A sustained drop in weight-for-age percentile appears weeks to months before clinical signs of illness or malnutrition, making regular growth monitoring a powerful early detection tool.

answers.text: It is specific to genetic growth disorders and confirms the diagnosis immediately

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Growth faltering is non-specific — it can result from nutritional, infective, psychosocial, or genetic causes. It flags a problem but does not confirm any particular diagnosis.

answers.text: It can only be identified through laboratory investigations such as serum albumin

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Growth faltering is detected by plotting serial anthropometric measurements on a growth chart, not through laboratory tests. This accessibility makes it valuable even in resource-limited settings.

overallFeedback.feedback: Growth faltering — a sustained drop in weight-for-age percentile — can be detected by serial weight plotting long before clinical signs of illness or malnutrition appear. This early detection is the core reason paediatric practice emphasises regular growth monitoring.
Exactly right. Growth faltering appears weeks to months before clinical signs, which is why routine growth monitoring at every paediatric contact is so important.

interactions.label: Glucocorticoids in excess promote growth in children by stimulating the growth p

params.question: Glucocorticoids in excess promote growth in children by stimulating the growth plates.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Glucocorticoids in excess suppress, not promote, growth in children. They inhibit the growth plates, which is why children on long-term corticosteroids (for conditions such as asthma or nephrotic syndrome) require regular growth monitoring.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Glucocorticoids in excess actually suppress growth by inhibiting the growth plates. This is clinically important in children on long-term corticosteroid therapy, where growth velocity must be carefully monitored.

interactions.label: A health worker at an Anganwadi centre measures a 30-month-old child lying flat

params.question: A health worker at an Anganwadi centre measures a 30-month-old child lying flat on a length board and records 87 cm. What is the most important error in this measurement?

answers.text: The child should have been measured standing, as children over two years require standing height measurement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. WHO standardised protocols require standing height for children aged two years and above. Recumbent length overestimates true height by approximately 0.7 cm, which can affect nutritional classification.

answers.text: The health worker should have used a weighing scale instead of a length board

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Length or height measurement is essential for assessing linear growth alongside weight. The error here is the measurement position, not the choice of instrument.

answers.text: The Frankfort horizontal plane cannot be maintained in the recumbent position, invalidating the reading

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Frankfort plane (aligning the lower orbital margin with the ear canal) can be maintained in both recumbent and standing positions. The error is using the recumbent position for a child over two years of age.

answers.text: Head circumference should have been measured instead of length at this age

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Head circumference and linear growth serve different purposes in growth assessment. Both remain relevant; the error here is the measurement position, not the parameter chosen.

overallFeedback.feedback: Children aged two years and above should be measured standing, not lying down. Recumbent length overestimates true height by about 0.7 cm — a seemingly small error that can shift a child's nutritional classification between categories.

Well done. Switching from recumbent length to standing height at two years is a key protocol step. The difference of approximately 0.7 cm may seem small, but it can shift a child between nutritional categories.

interactions.label: A child with Down syndrome raised in a supportive home with early intervention i

params.question: A child with Down syndrome raised in a supportive home with early intervention is compared to another child with the same condition who receives minimal stimulation. Which statement best reflects the gene–environment interaction in development?

answers.text: Both children will reach identical milestones because genetics alone determines developmental outcome

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While genetics sets biological constraints, developmental outcomes are significantly modulated by environmental factors such as stimulation and responsive caregiving. The same genetic condition can produce different outcomes in different environments.

answers.text: Environmental stimulation will completely compensate for the genetic condition, eliminating all delay

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Environmental stimulation cannot completely override a genetic condition like Down syndrome. It meaningfully improves the developmental trajectory, but some degree of delay will persist.

answers.text: The child receiving early intervention is likely to have a better developmental outcome across all domains

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Biological and environmental factors act together to determine developmental outcomes. A supportive environment with early intervention significantly improves outcomes in motor, language, social, and adaptive domains, even when a biological risk factor is present.

answers.text: Environmental factors influence only language development and have no effect on motor milestones

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Environmental stimulation influences all developmental domains — motor, language, social, and adaptive. A child who receives adequate stimulation and early intervention benefits across all domains, not just language.

overallFeedback.feedback: Biological and environmental factors interact to determine developmental outcomes. A genetic condition like Down syndrome sets constraints, but a supportive environment with early intervention significantly improves the child's trajectory across all domains — making identification of modifiable factors a key clinical responsibility.

Exactly right. The gene–environment interaction model is central to developmental paediatrics. Identifying and optimising modifiable environmental factors is one of the most impactful clinical actions for any child with developmental risk.
